name: London
seoTitle: Website Audit London — Free AI Website Health Check
metaDescription: Free AI website audit for London businesses. Find out why your site isn't winning more enquiries in one of the UK's most competitive search markets.
intro: London has the highest search competition of any UK market — for almost any local service, dozens of businesses are fighting for the same first page. A website that's merely "fine" doesn't survive that competition; small technical and SEO gaps are the difference between page one and page three.
painPoints: Competing against dozens of similar businesses across boroughs, where generic "London" targeting loses to competitors with borough-specific content (e.g. Hackney, Stratford, Croydon)
Higher visitor expectations for site speed and polish, since London audiences are used to slicker competitor sites and abandon slow ones faster
Local searches increasingly specifying a borough or postcode rather than just "London", missed entirely by sites without location-specific pages
Intense local SEO competition making Google Business Profile completeness and review volume a bigger differentiator than in less competitive markets

faq.question: Why isn't my business ranking in London even though my website looks fine?
faq.answer: London's search competition is intense enough that "fine" usually isn't enough — technical SEO gaps, thin local content, and page speed issues that wouldn't matter in a smaller market become the deciding factor here.

faq.question: Should I target specific London boroughs instead of just "London"?
faq.answer: Generally yes — borough or postcode-specific content (e.g. a dedicated page for Shoreditch or Croydon) lets you compete for more specific, less contested searches instead of the single hyper-competitive "London" term.

faq.question: How fast should my website be for London audiences?
faq.answer: The same Core Web Vitals benchmarks apply everywhere, but London visitors — used to slick competitor sites — tend to bounce from slow pages faster, making speed an even higher priority here than in less competitive markets.
